chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, and Al-Hajjaj, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Ma'mar ibn Umar, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the one upon whom clothing is obligated regarding the expiation of an oath. He (peace be upon him) said: 'A garment by which he covers his nakedness.'
ai.seo_question: What constitutes the required clothing for expiating an oath in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the minimal legal standard for the clothing component of kaffarat al-yamin, defining it merely as a garment sufficient to cover the awrah. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of avoiding undue hardship (raf' al-haraj), distinguishing the expiation's requirement from the more extensive clothing needed for prayer (salat). The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Kufan school through Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr and al-Hajjal.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, and Al Hajjaj, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Moamar Bin Umar who said,
‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the one upon whom is Obligated the clothing with regards to an expiation. He<sup>asws</sup> said:’ A cloth by which his nakedness is covered’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali has narrated from his father from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr and ai-Hajjai from Tha‘labah ibn Maymun from Mu’ammar ibn ‘Umar who has narrated the foliowing:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who must clothe the needy because of expiation due to oath. He (the Imam) said, ‘ It is a kind of clothing which can cover his privacy.’”
